item.title: Regulatory frameworks need to distinguish persistent from transient plastic fragments
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 16 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-03837-w

Plastic particles below a diameter of 5 mm are often grouped together under the label ‘microplastics’ in current Environmental Impact Assessment protocols, regardless of their environmental half-life. This Comment argues that microplastics should be regulated according to degradability, with separate categories for transient and persistent particles.
item.dc:title: Regulatory frameworks need to distinguish persistent from transient plastic fragments
item.dc:creator: Mirko Cucina

item.title: Abrupt permafrost thaw overwhelms vegetation-driven erosion reduction in sediment export on the Tibetan Plateau
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 16 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04125-3

Abrupt permafrost degradation through retrogressive thaw slumps can increase sediment delivery to Tibetan rivers, outweighing the greening-induced reduction in sediment export, suggests a study combining multi-decadal satellite observations, topographic differencing, and hydrological modelling.
item.dc:title: Abrupt permafrost thaw overwhelms vegetation-driven erosion reduction in sediment export on the Tibetan Plateau

item.title: Remote sensing of aquatic nutrients from proxy estimation to integration with process models
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04152-0

At the watershed scale, remote sensing maps land use and estimates pollution loads; at the lake scale, it provides water quality data for models; at field and interface scales, it identifies nutrient-loss hotspots, based on a review of remote sensing to approaches aquatic nutrients.
item.dc:title: Remote sensing of aquatic nutrients from proxy estimation to integration with process models

item.title: Nickel isotopes in Apollo and Chang’e soils reveal widespread micrometeorite-driven processing of the lunar regolith
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04139-x

Micrometeorite-driven processing causes widespread heavy Ni isotope enrichment across the lunar surface, although local signatures can be modified by regolith maturity and the addition of Ni-rich materials, according to Ni isotope analysis of lunar soils.
item.dc:title: Nickel isotopes in Apollo and Chang’e soils reveal widespread micrometeorite-driven processing of the lunar regolith

item.title: Seasonal wetting and drying dynamics drive greenhouse gas emissions across Australia’s river network
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04135-1

Australian rivers emit 48.5 teragrams of carbon dioxide and 0.28 teragrams of methane annually, with dry riverbeds adding 13.9 teragrams of carbon dioxide, according to integrated river emission measurements and geospatial drainage network analysis.
item.dc:title: Seasonal wetting and drying dynamics drive greenhouse gas emissions across Australia’s river network

item.title: Geochemical clustering reveals cryptic eruptions and tephra correlations from Antarctic fumarolic ice-cave archives
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04105-7

The identification of previously unrecognised eruptions and improved correlations between ice cave deposits and other volcanic archives refine the eruptive history of Mount Melbourne, according to geochemical analyses and statistical clustering of tephra from three Antarctic ice caves with existing volcanic records.
item.dc:title: Geochemical clustering reveals cryptic eruptions and tephra correlations from Antarctic fumarolic ice-cave archives

item.title: Global ice loss drives source-independent amplification of sea-level rise at Pacific and Indian Ocean Small Island Developing States
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04132-4

Many Pacific and Indian Ocean small island developing states are located within persistent sea-level-rise hotspots, according to glacier mass flux and sea level projections.
item.dc:title: Global ice loss drives source-independent amplification of sea-level rise at Pacific and Indian Ocean Small Island Developing States
